plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: Enormous, ruffled, fragrant blooms unfold like silk pom-poms in shades of blush, rose and crimson. They sit above glossy, deeply cut foliage in cottage gardens and parks.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring, typically May to early June, with peak bloom often around mid to late May in temperate regions
plants.location: Temperate Northern Hemisphere gardens, including the northern United States, Europe and northern China, where the species is native
plants.funFact: Peony buds are often covered in sweet nectar that attracts ants. Despite an old myth, the ants are not needed for the flowers to open.

plants.name: Rosa gallica
plants.description: One of the oldest cultivated roses, it has richly scented, semi-double flowers in deep pinks and purple-crimson. Golden stamens glow at the center of each bloom.
plants.bloomingSeason: Once-blooming in late spring to early summer, usually May to June in temperate Europe
plants.location: Central and southern Europe, and gardens across the temperate Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Gallica roses are among the ancestors of many modern garden roses, and their petals keep their fragrance for a long time after drying.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This is an evergreen shrub with glossy leaves and delicate, silky blossoms. In the cool, misty Southern Hemisphere autumn it brightens gardens when most other plants are fading.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter, roughly April to July in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Cultivated gardens in Australia, New Zealand and South Africa, and native to southern Japan
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is related to the tea plant, Camellia sinensis, and its seeds are pressed for an edible oil used in parts of Asia.
